key_insight: A synchronized multi-camera platform and real-time 3D tracking pipeline can overcome persistent occlusion and rapid state changes, enabling reliable multiadic (multiple humans and robots) interaction in realistic home environments.
problem_solved: Addresses the bottleneck of robust real-time 3D tracking for close-proximity, concurrent human–robot interactions in cluttered, occlusion-heavy home settings—necessary for safe, coordinated multiadic collaboration.
method: Distributed, synchronized multi-camera capture network to provide dense, overlapping views and reduce persistent occlusions.
Real-time multi-view 3D fusion and tracking algorithms with occlusion-aware data association to maintain consistent object and human state under rapid motion and close contact.
Integrated hardware–software platform that combines cameras, processing pipeline, and robot interfaces to support concurrent multi-human, multi-robot tasks and enable reproducible experiments.
impact: Enables researchers and engineers to develop and evaluate multiadic HRI systems that are robust to occlusion and temporal coupling, accelerating progress on safe, scalable home robotics and real-time perception models.
visual_elements: System architecture diagram showing camera network, real-time fusion pipeline, and robot/human actors
Interaction timeline illustrating concurrent, interleaved subtasks between multiple humans and robots
Before/after multi-view reconstructions or frames highlighting occlusion reduction and tracking continuity
Performance chart (e.g., tracking accuracy vs. occlusion level or latency vs. robustness) to quantify real-time behavior
paper_title: OmniRobotHome: A Multi-Camera Platform for Real-Time Multiadic Human-Robot Interaction
paper_authors: Junyoung Lee, Sookwan Han, Jeonghwan Kim, Inhee Lee, Mingi Choi
